stanzas: אֵין לוֹ דְמוּת הַגּוּף וְאֵינוֹ גוּף
orig.credit: Medieval Hebrew hymn, its author disputed

stanzas: Exalted be the living God and praised;
he exists, and there is no time bounding his existence.
One, and there is no oneness like his oneness;
hidden, and there is also no end to his unity.
He has no likeness of a body, and he is not a body;
we cannot set his holiness beside him [?].
Prior to every thing that was created,
first, and there is no beginning to his beginning.
Behold, he is Lord of the world to every creature;
he shows his greatness and his kingship.
The flow of his prophecy he gave to
the men of his treasured portion and his glory.
There has not arisen again in Israel one like Moses,
a prophet who beholds his likeness.
A Torah of truth God gave to his people
by the hand of his prophet, the trusted one of his house.
God will not exchange nor alter
his law, for all ages, for any other.
He watches and knows our secrets;
he sees the end of a thing at its beginning.
He repays a man with kindness according to his deed;
he gives the wicked evil according to his wickedness.
He will send at the end of days our anointed one
to redeem those who wait for the end, his salvation.
The dead God will bring to life in his great kindness;
blessed for ever and ever be the name of his praise.
en lo demut haguf veeno guf

notes: The hymn sets out the Thirteen Principles of Maimonides, one or two to a line.
line 3.2: 'lo naarokh elav qedushato' is read as 'we cannot compare his holiness to anything' or 'we cannot describe his holiness'; the construction is compressed.
line 12.1: 'yamin' here is the poetic form of 'yamim', 'days', not 'right hand'.
line 12.2: 'qets yeshuato': 'the end (the appointed time) of his salvation'.
